question.problem:
Which of the following geometric series converge?

I. ${\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{{6}^{n-1}}{{12}^{n}}$

II. ${\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }5{(\frac{2}{3})}^{n}$

III. ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{(\frac{4}{3})}^{n}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's look at each series in turn.

- The series ${\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{{6}^{n-1}}{{12}^{n}}$ starts with $n=3.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{4}}{{a}_{3}} & =\frac{(\frac{{6}^{4-1}}{{12}^{4}})}{(\frac{{6}^{3-1}}{{12}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{6}^{3}}{{12}^{4}})}{(\frac{{6}^{2}}{{12}^{3}})} \\  & =(\frac{{6}^{3}}{{12}^{4}})(\frac{{12}^{3}}{{6}^{2}}) \\  & =(\frac{6}{12}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is convergent because $|r|<1.$

- The series ${\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }5{(\frac{2}{3})}^{n}$ starts with $n=2.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{3}}{{a}_{2}} & =\frac{5{(\frac{2}{3})}^{3}}{5{(\frac{2}{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is convergent because $|r|<1.$

- The series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{(\frac{4}{3})}^{n}$ starts with $n=1.$ So the common ratio is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}} & =\frac{{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2}}{{(\frac{4}{3})}^{1}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the series is divergent because $|r|\ge 1.$

In conclusion, only series I and II converge.
